name: drg-0006-goal2
goal: Measure the size of each neuron and report how many are large (more than 40 µm across).

look.notes: The image is a fluorescence microscopy image of a rat dorsal root ganglion section stained with an antibody against neurofilament, a neuronal marker. The structures visible are neurons and their processes. The total number of neurons is estimated to be around 10,000 based on the scale and density. The images are at different magnifications (whole section, detail 1, detail 2) with pixel sizes corresponding to 1.66 µm, 0.52 µm, and 0.52 µm respectively.

not_possible: The goal requires measuring the size of each neuron and counting those larger than 40 µm. While the image is fluorescence and shows neurons stained with neurofilament, the resolution and scale are insufficient to accurately measure individual neuron sizes (pixel size 1.04 µm, but magnifications vary). The tools available (e.g., find_cells, measure) are designed for object measurement, but the image lacks the resolution to reliably distinguish individual neurons or measure their diameters with precision. The tools cannot reliably segment or measure neurons at the required scale without additional data or higher-resolution imaging.

steps.why: This tool can outline and measure neurons based on their morphology and staining. It will attempt to identify and measure the size of each neuron in the image, which is necessary to determine which are larger than 40 µm.
This tool will measure the size (diameter or area) of each neuron identified by find_cells. It will be used to determine which neurons are larger than 40 µm.
This tool will count the number of neurons that are larger than 40 µm, based on the measurements from the measure tool.

plan.result: The analysis will attempt to measure the size of each neuron and count those larger than 40 µm. However, due to the resolution and scale of the image, the measurements may be inaccurate or unreliable, leading to potential under- or over-estimation of neuron sizes and counts.
risks: The resolution of the image (pixel size 1.04 µm) is insufficient to accurately measure individual neuron sizes, especially at the 40 µm threshold. This could lead to misclassification of neurons as large or small.
The tools may not be able to reliably segment individual neurons due to overlapping or indistinct boundaries, leading to inaccurate measurements and counts.
The image may not contain enough neurons to make the analysis statistically significant, or the neurons may be too densely packed to be accurately measured.
